claim: Which hydroxyl of the glycerol carries the adamantylacetyl group
locus_A: Appendix S1 p.2: intermediate 4 is named "(R)-3-(2-(adamantan-1-yl)acetoxy)-2-hydroxypropyl ... phosphate" (adamantylacetyl at C3, free OH at C2), made by "dibutyltin oxide-mediated selective PRIMARY alcohol acylation"; eight of the ten products are named the same way
locus_B: Appendix S1 pp.3-4: A-10 is named "(R)-2-(2-(adamantan-1-yl)acetoxy)-3-(undecanoyloxy)propyl ..." and A-11 "(R)-2-(2-(adamantan-1-yl)acetoxy)-3-(dodecanoyloxy)propyl ..." -- the two acyl groups SWAPPED
what_we_emitted: All ten built with adamantylacetyl on the PRIMARY (C3) hydroxyl and the fatty acyl on the secondary (C2) hydroxyl
why: The route decides it: 4 is made by selective primary acylation and its own printed name puts the adamantylacetyl at C3; the Steglich step then acylates the one remaining OH, at C2. All ten 1H NMR spectra show the same pattern (a 1H multiplet at 5.13-5.21 for an esterified C2 methine, plus a 4.37 dd), so the series is homogeneous. MASS CANNOT SEE THIS: measured, the two regioisomers of A-11 have identical formula C32H58NO8P and identical exact mass 615.390004 Da, delta 0.000000. Seed S5 confirms the HRMS gate runs GREEN on the swapped build; seed G3 confirms the InChIKey anchor gate catches it (0/2 agreements). A-11 is the paper's LEAD compound (LNP1), so this is not a cosmetic naming point.

claim: How many phospholipids the esterification afforded, and where the series starts
locus_A: Results: "afforded 10 compounds, A-10 to A-17-2Z"; Figure 1a product box labelled "A10-17-2Z"
locus_B: Figure 1b (10 tail IDs: 9,10,11,12,13,14,15,16,17,17-2Z), Figure 1c (10 tabulated compounds beginning at A-9), Figures 2d/3f/3h (10 bars each, first bar A-9), and Appendix S1 p.2 which gives a full procedure for A-9 at 92% yield
why: The count "10" and the range "A-10 to A-17-2Z" contradict each other inside one sentence: that range holds nine compounds. Figure 1a prints the yield range "77-92%" for the same box, and we measured it against the ten isolated yields: min 77 and max 92 reproduce the printed range EXACTLY, while A-10..A-17-2Z alone gives 77-89. 92% is A-9 yield and no other compound of the ten. So A-9 belongs to the series and the range START is the typo. This is a number the authors printed and never computed.

locus_A: Appendix S1 p.7: "HRMS (ESI, m/z) calcd for C37H68NO8P [M + Na]+: 708.4575" -- a formula with no sodium, against an [M+Na]+ adduct
locus_B: Figure 1c prints A-16 NEUTRAL formula as C37H68NO8P; our C37H68NNaO8P+ reproduces the printed 708.4575 to -0.02 mDa
what_we_emitted: Neutral C37H68NO8P; sodium adduct C37H68NNaO8P+ at 708.4575
why: The SI pasted the neutral formula into the adduct slot. Decided from the NUMBER, not from preference: the printed mass is the sodiated one and matches ours, and Fig 1c independently prints the same neutral formula. Only the SI formula STRING is wrong; the structure and the mass are right. (The AC_2025 lesson: repairing the wrong half of a name/structure disagreement once moved 419 measured values onto the wrong molecules.)

locus_B: The same column homologous steps: A-12 -> A-13 is 13.0 Da and A-13 -> A-14 is 15.0 Da, where every other step in the saturated series is 13.9-14.2 (CH2 = 14.027). Our average MW is 643.84 against a median printed offset of -0.435 Da, leaving A-13 a 1.0 Da residual where every other compound is under 0.1
why: A one-digit typo in the printed table: 643.4 was set as 642.4. The two anomalous steps sum to exactly 28.0 = 2 x CH2, the signature of a single mis-set digit rather than a wrong structure. A-13 FORMULA is right in Fig 1c, right in the SI HRMS, and its printed [M+H]+ calcd 644.4286 reproduces ours exactly. The step test is internal to the paper: it uses only the authors' own column and would find this even if our build were wrong.

locus_A: Results: "the amount of individual barcode N divided by the sum of all barcodes in that cell type, for all N barcodes" -- a plain composition
locus_B: Methods 3.11: "Counts for each particle, per tissue, were normalized to the barcoded LNP mixture we injected into the mouse. This input DNA provided the DNA counts and was used to normalize DNA counts from the cells and tissues" -- an input-ratio normalisation
why: The two descriptions are different formulas, and the paper publishes NO worked example and no counts, so the normalisation cannot be reconstructed and NO RESIDUAL CAN BE REPORTED. Which family it belongs to IS decidable: both plotted axes centre on 1 (Fig 3c logarithmic 0.1-10; Fig 3f/3g 0.00-1.25 with bars at 0.65-1.02), whereas a plain composition over 109 LNPs would centre on 1/109 = 0.00917, about 94-109x lower. So the readout is compositional in ORIGIN and then rescaled against the injected input -- the Methods description -- and the Results sentence is an incomplete paraphrase of it.

claim: Which sterol and which molar ratio LNP1 uses
locus_A: Results and Fig 3i identify LNP1 only as "an individual LNP formulated with phospholipid A-11"
locus_B: Fig 2a/2b establish that every LNP in the study is one of 3 sterols x 4 molar ratios, so LNP1 must be one specific combination of the 12
why: The paper never states LNP1 sterol or molar ratio, anywhere in the main text, the figures or Appendix S1. Fig 3h reports A-11 enrichment pooled over sterols, so even the screen's own analysis does not single one out. CHL_name, CHL_SMILES and all four *_molratio columns would have to be guessed, and CLAUDE.md section 7 forbids that. This is why the one individually-injected, individually-measured LNP in the paper is still not emittable -- on top of its ionizable lipid being the same cKK-E15 as every other LNP.
